clue.text: One seldom coming out of his shell

definitions.text: One seldom coming out of his shell

parts.words: One seldom coming out of his shell
parts.note: reads like a shy recluse who rarely socialises, but describes a crustacean living in a borrowed shell

explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean lives inside an abandoned whelk shell and retreats into it, like a recluse who keeps to himself.

clue.text: Injury not agreeable, unless taking on IOUs

indicators.note: read as 'less' plus 'taking', telling us to take some letters away from the word for agreeable

parts.note: agreeable means harmonious, getting along well
the word on followed by IOUs, written out as letters

explanation.surface: Being hurt is no fun unless someone takes on your debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unless taking' splits as 'un-less': remove ON plus IOUS from HARMONIOUS (agreeable) to leave the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or hurt done to someone, a synonym of injury.

clue.text: It's 'invariably a matter of course

parts.note: describes something done the same way every time as a regular habit

explanation.definitionFit: A fixed, habitual procedure is followed every time as standard practice.

clue.text: Depressed areas

parts.note: sounds like regions in economic decline, but means places pushed in, hollows or notches in a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Notches and dents are places where a surface has been pressed inwards.

clue.text: About one hundred and fifty sugar lumps in compartments

indicators.note: the sugar lumps come about, going around the other letters to enclose them

parts.note: sugar lumps are sugar cubes
one is the Roman numeral I
C is a hundred and L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Roughly 150 sugar lumps stored away in little boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' leads the clue but is the container signal, wrapping the sugar lumps round the Roman numerals; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small partitioned sections of a room, such as changing booths, are compartments.

clue.text: Peter Pan would never be one of them

definitions.text: Peter Pan would never be one of them

parts.words: Peter Pan would never be one of them
parts.note: the boy who never grew up refuses to become a grown-up

explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups are what Peter Pan, the boy who would not grow up, refused to become.

clue.text: A call to them might provoke a breach of the peace

definitions.text: A call to them might provoke a breach of the peace

parts.words: A call to them might provoke a breach of the peace
parts.note: a 'call to' these is a summons to take up weapons, which certainly ends peace

explanation.definitionFit: Weapons are what a call to battle summons people to take up.

clue.text: Dare one break into a girls' school?

indicators.note: to break the words is to smash them up and reassemble the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Would anyone be bold enough to burgle a girls' school?
explanation.walkthrough: ROEDEAN is a famous girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known English independent boarding school for girls.

clue.text: Most beloved of Lear's little dogs

definitions.meaning: a person dearest of all, a darling
in King Lear the mad king names his little dogs Tray, Blanch and one more

explanation.surface: The favourite among King Lear's pet dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Lear cries 'The little dogs and all, Tray, Blanch and Sweetheart, see, they bark at me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is one's most beloved, and Shakespeare gives that same pet name to one of Lear's dogs.

clue.text: Revolver kept in fair condition ?

parts.note: looks like a gun kept in decent order, but means a revolving ride kept at a funfair

explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is a revolving ride found at a fairground.

clue.text: Present the first half of the wake

indicators.note: only the opening half of the name is wanted, the first four letters of eight

parts.note: Hereward the Wake, the English hero who resisted the Norman conquest

explanation.surface: A gift made during the early part of a funeral vigil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wake' is not a vigil but the epithet of Hereward the Wake, the eleventh-century rebel against William the Conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present means being in this place, at hand.

clue.text: One criminally prone to woolgathering ?

parts.note: woolgathering usually means daydreaming, here taken literally as gathering wool illegally, from flocks

explanation.definitionFit: A rustler of flocks illegally takes woolly animals, literally gathering wool.

clue.text: Foreigner suffering a loss — right?

indicators.note: the foreigner loses a, the letter named in the indicator phrase

parts.note: a foreigner is an alien

explanation.surface: An outsider who has been bereaved: is that correct?
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is a right to hold someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Hydrographical area for slip-fielders ?

parts.note: a drainage basin, punningly read as a place for the cricketers stationed in the slips, whose job is to hold catches

explanation.walkthrough: Slip fielders in cricket stand beside the wicketkeeper to take catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainage basin is the region from which rainfall collects into a river.

clue.text: It was a great relief to cause this outburst

definitions.text: It was a great relief to cause this outburst

parts.words: It was a great relief to cause this outburst
parts.note: the relief of Mafeking in 1900 set off wild street celebrations in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' is not comfort but the lifting of the siege of Mafeking in the Boer War; the riotous rejoicing that followed gave English a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous public rejoicing is named after the London celebrations of the lifting of the Mafeking siege.

clue.text: Means tests for cricketers ?

definitions.meaning: arithmetic means, the sum divided by the count
a cricketer's runs per innings or runs conceded per wicket measure his worth

explanation.definitionFit: Mean values are arithmetic figures, and batting and bowling figures of this sort judge a cricketer.

clue.text: Held in the sitting-room, of course

definitions.text: Held in the sitting-room, of course

parts.words: Held in the sitting-room, of course
parts.note: a 'sitting' is a gathering to contact spirits, and the French word for it means a sitting

explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist meeting is called a sitting, which is what the French word literally means.

clue.text: They sound anti-song as well as anti-law

definitions.text: They sound anti-song as well as anti-law

parts.words: They sound anti-song as well as anti-law
parts.note: outlaws whose name said aloud is like 'ban ditty', a prohibition on a song

explanation.definitionFit: Bandits or outlaws are against the law, and the plural Italian form sounds like 'ban ditty'.

clue.text: The old person was naturally petrified

definitions.text: The old person was naturally petrified

parts.words: The old person was naturally petrified
parts.note: an old-fashioned person is called by the name of remains turned to stone by nature

explanation.definitionFit: A preserved prehistoric organism has been turned to stone, and an old fogey gets the same name.

clue.text: US legislator's terrible treason

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A member of Congress commits dreadful betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (is) between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US upper house of Congress is a legislator.

clue.text: Transitory feast ?

parts.note: a festival named for an angel passing by Israelite houses, so 'transitory' in the sense of going past

explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish festival commemorates the angel of death passing by the Israelites' homes.

clue.text: Archdeacon's performing with the meat

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven, and the 's stands for is
a performer who is on stage is performing

explanation.surface: A clergyman is on stage, sharing the bill with the roast.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is addressed as 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh is the meat sold under this name.

clue.text: Regard in a favourable light

parts.note: to look on someone with approval and respect

explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high respect is to regard them favourably.

clue.text: Deacons in saintly array

indicators.note: to array is to set out in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'array' looks like clothing but is the anagram signal, applied to DEACONS and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being declared a saint by the Church makes one officially saintly.

clue.text: Is she indeed nameless? Yes and no

indicators.note: she is and is not nameless: her name sits inside the words, so it is both there and not shown

explanation.surface: A coy question whether a woman truly has no name, answered evasively.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name runs across the end of 'indeed' and the start of 'nameless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so a person referred to as she.

clue.text: Love is aggrieved, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aggrieved person is sore about it

explanation.surface: A lover who has been wronged is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love personifies desire.

clue.text: Nine letters returned — one from Greece

definitions.text: Nine letters returned — one from Greece

parts.words: Nine letters returned — one from Greece
parts.note: counting through the Greek alphabet, the ninth letter is a single Greek character

explanation.definitionFit: The ninth character of the Greek alphabet is a letter from Greece.

clue.text: Whereby land can be put right, if sterile

definitions.text: Whereby land can be put right, if sterile

indicators.note: the letters can be put another way, set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: How barren farmland is restored to health.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: 'can be put' rearranges IF STERILE, and R (right) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure or chemical nutrients restore barren soil, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: Clothes can become worthless with age

indicators.note: these letters plus a word become the word for worthless, so that word is taken away to recover them

parts.note: worthless stuff is rubbish, garbage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Old clothes eventually turn into rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the clothes word plus AGE gives the rubbish word, so remove AGE from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments or attire, especially distinctive dress, are clothes.

clue.text: They, don't object to being taken in

definitions.text: They, don't object to being taken in

parts.words: They, don't object to being taken in
parts.note: sounds like gullible people happy to be fooled, but means newcomers glad to be admitted to a country

explanation.definitionFit: Settlers arriving in a new country want to be admitted and welcomed.
